subject: Post-demo: Integration assembly & orchestration checklist (MAP draft)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex@cloudhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Integration assembly & orchestration checklist (MAP draft)

Dana / Alex — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a focused next step: I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (CHA_MAP_v0.2.xlsx) and an SDK integration checklist (pdf) that isolate the build milestones we discussed.

High-level asks from CloudHealth: streaming generation + tool-calling, structured JSON outputs for billing reconciliation, and an SDK embed path for their agent. On our side the key milestones are: 1) SDK integration + auth flow, 2) streaming + KV cache behavior tests, 3) tool-calling hooks and security review, 4) structured output schema and evals.

I've populated owners where we talked them through — please review and flag any changes. Proposed target close for the MAP: 2027-05-20 (customer lock and first pilot).

Immediate next step: Can you confirm the dependency below so we can lock milestone owners?
- Customer to provide a sandbox project with sample dataset and service account for auth by 2027-04-18
- Redwood to produce a streaming test harness and SDK starter repo by 2027-04-29

Attachments: CHA_MAP_v0.2.xlsx (MAP draft), sdk_integration_checklist.pdf

Thanks — I looped in Marissa and Dev to own implementation work and Laura as the renewal lead.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182
From: Dana Morris <dana.morris@cloudhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex@cloudhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:02:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Integration assembly & orchestration checklist (MAP draft)

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful. Two quick clarifications from our engineering team: 
1) For the SDK auth path, do you support both short-lived service account tokens and a long-lived API-key mode? Our infra prefers short-lived tokens (we can provide keybroker) but procurement will want an API-key fallback.
2) For streaming behavior, what SLOs should we expect for 1k concurrent user sessions? We need a baseline to size our pilot cluster.

On dates: sandbox by 4/18 is doable but we need an internal security review before sharing service accounts — that could add 3 business days. Would you be open to a 4/20 buffer for the sandbox if necessary?

Dana Morris
Head of Integrations, CloudHealth Analytics
dana.morris@cloudhealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@cloudhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Integration assembly & orchestration checklist (MAP draft)

Hi Dana — quick answers and owner notes: 
- Auth modes: Rishi, we can support both modes. Marissa (solutions) + Dev (platform) will document the short-lived token flow and the API-key fallback in the checklist.
- Streaming SLOs: preliminary baseline for 1k concurrent streaming sessions depends heavily on prompt length and token/sec; ballpark numbers: 95th pct latency ~300–450ms for 256-token windows on a dedicated NPU-backed pool. I'll put a conservative pilot target in the MAP.

I'll update CHA_MAP_v0.2 with: owner columns, explicit dependency on sandbox+IAM, and a pilot sizing appendix.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dana Morris <dana.morris@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: vendor-sdk@acme.dev, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 12:34:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Integration assembly & orchestration checklist (MAP draft)

Looping in a quick technical note from the implementation side:
- SDK starter repo: I'll publish a typescript and python starter by 4/29. It will include an auth adapter for service-account short-lived tokens (exchanges via our Key Broker) and a simple API-key shim for local dev.
- Tool-calling: we'll expose a declarative hook interface (webhook + signed call) and recommend an outbound proxy for customer tool endpoints behind their VPC. Security review: need the threat model doc from CloudHealth (link in the MAP) and any allowed IP ranges for whitelist testing.

On structured outputs: we propose shipping an initial JSON schema (billing_records.v0) for review; Marissa will coordinate sample mappings.

Attachments referenced: draft_kb_flow.drawio (internal), starter_repo_README.md (stub)

— Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@cloudhealth.com>, Alex Rivera <alex@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Integration assembly & orchestration checklist (MAP draft)

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turns. Summary and commit: 
- New MAP version: CHA_MAP_v0.3 (I will upload after Marissa's owner column and Dev's starter repo link are in).
- Dependencies: CloudHealth sandbox + threat model by 2027-04-20 (accepting the 4/20 buffer).
- Milestone owners: SDK integration = Dev Patel; Streaming tests = Marissa Cole; Tool-calling & security review = Dev Patel; Pilot evaluation & renewal ops = Laura Bennett.
- Target MAP close: 2027-05-20. Pilot go/no-go checkpoint: 2027-06-07.

Next immediate step: Dana, please confirm you can share the sandbox contact (or a directory for our SRE) by 4/20 and we'll schedule a 45-minute kickoff for the build owners the week of 4/25.

Onward — I'll update the MAP and push to the Drive.

— Rishi
